subject: Kickoff: Wasserstein batch-effect correction as a corpus-wide layer
body:
Team,

Starting this one today. Our open-source release corrects batch effects in high-content imaging embeddings by minimizing a Wasserstein distance between batch distributions, validated on the BBBC021 set with both CellProfiler embeddings and deep-network embeddings.

My interest is broader than cell imaging. Every embedding corpus we own has nuisance structure - collection run, labeling wave, vendor - and today teams paper over it with ad hoc normalization. If the Wasserstein approach transfers, it becomes a standard de-batching step in the corpus pipeline rather than a biology trick.

Mar 30 - Jul 6. Milestones:
- Apr 24: reproduce the paper on BBBC021, both embedding types, using the ljosa preprocessing path.
- May 29: apply to one non-imaging Meridian corpus, measure whether downstream retrieval improves.
- Jun 26: go/no-go on productizing as a Corpus pipeline stage.

Alina on resourcing, Umar tech lead.

Anders
